item.title: Watch Celtics’ Jayson Tatum reveal his stunned reaction to the Jaylen Brown trade
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Watch Celtics’ Jayson Tatum reveal his stunned reaction to the Jaylen Brown trade appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Boston Celtics star Jayson Tatum revealed that he learned about Jaylen Brown the same way fans learned about the trade, from ESPN’s Shams Charania. Tatum addressed his relationship with Brown after the trade with the Philadelphia 76ers, weeks after the blockbuster swap involving Paul George. This time, though, he went into great detail. In a recent epsiode of his vlog, Tatum revealed when he first found out about Brown’s trade to the 76ers, per Celtics Wire’s Daniel Donabedian. “We was in Vegas. I just got done playing pick-up the first day. Shams walks over. He hand me the towel and he’s like, “Yo, put this over your face. Don’t react. They just traded him.” I’m like, ‘Oh s***,’ I’m like, ‘Where?’ He said, “Philly.” You traded him down the street? So, I was just as much off-guard as the rest of the world,” Tatum said. “I very much have been transparent about how thankful, I personally am, for our relationship, and what we were able to accomplish over nine years. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Talk about 2017 to 2025-26. Jayson and Jaylen. You won’t ever be able to talk about one of us without the other. Just our ability to grow up as kids. And go through our ups and downs. And people talking about one of us had to go. And we couldn’t win together. There was a lot of s*** that we had to deal with.” After Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown led the Celtics to a championship in 2024, the Celtics forward knows their legacy is forever cemented together. “I will always say I knew every time I stepped on that court that when it was time to go to war, I looked to my left and my right and number 7 was over there, I knew that he was going to do whatever it took for us to try to win,” Tatum added. “The way we pushed each other. I definitely made him better and he made me better. And we made our team better. We made this organization better. We won a championship. We are forever stitched in stone in NBA history. We held up that trophy. It won’t ever be forgotten.” Jayson Tatum’s initial reaction to the Celtics trading Jaylen Brown: “You traded him down the street?” (h/t @danield1214 ) pic.twitter.com/zZd5GCkhzp — Legion Hoops (@LegionHoops) October 22, 2026 Tatum and the Celtics will face Brown and the 76ers for the first time this season on the road on November 10. item.title: Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield reveals Steelers goal he missed before return from thumb injury
item.description: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield reveals Steelers goal he missed before return from thumb injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Baker Mayfield had his eyes on a return against the Pittsburgh Steelers, but the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback knew his right thumb was not ready. Mayfield dislocated the thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings when his throwing hand hit linebacker Blake Cashman on a late fourth-down pass. He has missed the last three games since then, with undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels starting in his place. Speaking to reporters on Thursday , Mayfield admitted he pushed his recovery to try to play against Pittsburgh, per ESPN’s Jenna Laine. He eventually decided that Daniels gave the Buccaneers a better chance to win. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Yeah, my goal was Pittsburgh, to be honest with you. I really, really pushed the limit on it and wasn’t able to do it, didn’t feel like I was gonna put our team in a position to have success. Felt like Jalon was gonna be the better option, and so pushed it, and you don’t know until you try it. So this, obviously, with the goal of Pittsburgh and understanding we have two division games right after that, we can settle for that. Obviously, I want to be up there and play with the guys, but yeah, this was kind of the last week that I wanted to be ready to roll,” Mayfield said. Baker Mayfield said his goal was actually to return for Pittsburgh but he felt he wasn’t 100% and Jalon gave them a better chance to win. pic.twitter.com/GfQZNRD85Z — JennaLaineESPN (@JennaLaineESPN) October 22, 2026 The answer came after a reporter noted that head coach Todd Bowles had talked about a minimum of three games for Mayfield’s absence. The Steelers game did not go Tampa Bay’s way. The Buccaneers blew a 16-3 fourth-quarter lead and lost 26-19 in overtime , with Daniels throwing two fourth-quarter interceptions that led to Pittsburgh field goals. Daniels went 1-2 as the starter, highlighted by a win over the Dallas Cowboys on Oct. 8. Mayfield praised the rookie for how he handled being “thrown into the fire.” Now, Mayfield is expected to start Sunday against the Carolina Panthers , barring any setbacks. He was a full participant in practice on Wednesday and Thursday and plans to wear a custom glove with a reinforced pad to protect the thumb. The timing matters for Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers sit at 1-5 and last in the NFC South, while the Panthers lead the division at 3-2. The Buccaneers will need more from their franchise quarterback if they want to climb back into the race . item.title: Huntington scores late to slip past Captain Shreve on senior night
item.description: Captain Shreve said goodbye to 17 seniors playing their final regular season game at Lee Hedges as the home team Thursday night, but Huntington made sure it was a disappointing finale with a 28-21 win. After a poor special teams effort by the Gators with about 2 minutes remaining, Huntington quarterback Braylon Washington scored on a 23-yard run for the game-winner . Washington had scored earlier in the fourth quarter on a 3-yard run to knot the game at 21. The game ended with a Gator pass missing in the end zone. Washington finished with 73 yards passing and 27 yards rushing with the two scores. The win solidified the Raiders’ chances at a postseason berth, while the loss by the Gators severed a two-game winning streak and put doubt on their ability to host a first-round playoff game. The Raiders (2-6) got on the board late in the first quarter when AJ Johnson cashed in on a 2-yard drive. Shreve’s Gage Lockett answered for the Gators (4-4) with his 5-yard TD run with about 6 minutes to play in the first half. And Shreve took the lead with just 50 seconds remaining in the half when Maddox Parrott found Chris Hill for a 42-yard TD pass down the left sideline. PREDICTIONS: Find out which Shreveport-area football teams should win Week 8 games WEEK 8 SLATE: Here’s the 2026 Week 8 schedule for Shreveport-area football teams The Raiders came out of the locker room and put together a long drive, capped by a 13-yard TD run by Johnson to go in front 14-13. The Gators couldn’t get much going offensively in the second half until the fourth quarter when Lockett scored on a 5-yard run and Parrott ran in the 2-point conversion for a 21-14 Shreve lead with 8:24 to play. Huntington answered quickly with a short drive to tie the game at 21 on Washington’s first TD run with under 4 minutes remaining in regulation. Shreve did post 401 yards of offense with Lockett rushing for 103 yards and two TDs. Parrott passed for 245 yards and one TD with 61 more rushing yards. Jonesboro-Hodge 36, Montgomery 6: The Tigers (6-2) outplayed Montgomery (4-4) from start to finish to take charge in the district race. item.title: Raiders TE Brock Bowers gets eye-opening upgrade on injury report before Rams game
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Candice Ward-Imagn Images Raiders TE Brock Bowers gets eye-opening upgrade on injury report before Rams game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Las Vegas Raiders tight end Brock Bowers returned to full participation at Thursday’s practice, a welcome development for the team ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams . Bowers was limited on Wednesday because of hamstring and calf injuries . He missed the first two games of the 2026 season after undergoing a minor knee procedure shortly before the campaign began. His latest injury report designation is the first time this season he has been listed with an issue other than his knee. Through four appearances, Bowers has recorded 28 receptions for 382 yards and three touchdowns. He has also produced two 100-yard receiving performances this season. During Las Vegas’ 33-30 loss to the Buffalo Bills last week, he caught four passes on nine targets for 70 yards. That contest was the first time this season he failed to receive double-digit targets. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bowers’ return to full practice participation comes as the Raiders attempt to end a three-game losing streak. Over their past three games, Las Vegas has been outscored 64-41 after halftime, including a 24-3 disadvantage in the third quarter. The Raiders have also committed seven second-half turnovers this season, with four of quarterback Kirk Cousins’ five interceptions occurring during the final two quarters. Las Vegas has shown offensive potential, averaging 26.7 points per game, the sixth-highest mark in the league. However, inconsistent red-zone execution and defensive woes have prevented the Raiders from consistently closing out games. Alongside Bowers, defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi and offensive tackle Kolton Miller also returned to full participation after being limited Wednesday. Defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway was limited after missing the previous practice, while running back Mike Washington did not participate and linebacker Quay Walker remained limited. item.title: Patriots playoff picture: How loss to Bears impacts AFC standings
item.description: The New England Patriots came up short on Thursday Night Football, losing 30-24 to the Chicago Bears . Besides putting an end to the team’s three-game winning streak, the defeat also impacts its standing in the AFC playoff picture. With the majority of Week 7 games left to be played, the Patriots now find themselves out of the postseason slots. AFC East standings Buffalo Bills (5-1) New England Patriots (4-2) New York Jets (2-4) Miami Dolphins (0-5) The Patriots remain in second place in their division even after losing to the Bears, and would have stayed put regardless of what the weekend slate would have brought. The Bills, after all, are on a bye, meaning New England would not have overtaken them even in case of a win. That said, what was a one-game deficit entering Thursday is now a 1.5-game gap that needs to be overcome. AFC playoff standings Kansas City Chiefs (5-0) Buffalo Bills (5-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (4-2) Cleveland Browns (4-2) Denver Broncos (4-2) Pittsburgh Steelers (4-2) Baltimore Ravens (4-2) On the bubble: 8. Cincinnati Bengals (3-2) , 9. New England Patriots (4-3) , 10. Las Vegas Raiders (3-3), 11. New York Jets (2-4), 12. Indianapolis Colts (2-4), 13. Houston Texans (2-4 ), 14. Tennessee Titans (1-5) Not yet eliminated, but let’s be real here: 15. Miami Dolphins (0-5), 16. Los Angeles Chargers (0-6) As mentioned earlier, the Patriots are currently out of the playoff picture. In fact, they made a sizable drop from the fifth to the ninth position in the standings. They will overtake at least one other team again, however, given that the Ravens and Bengals are going against each other on Sunday. To reenter the playoff spots before the end of Week 7, however, New England will need other games to go in its favor as well.

item.title: Ducks bedeviled again on the road, drop 5th straight
item.description: Oct 22, 2026; Newark, New Jersey, USA; Anaheim Ducks center Tim Washe (42) tries to gain control of the puck against New Jersey Devils center Dawson Mercer (91) during the first half at Prudential Center. NEWARK, N.J. – It was deja vu all over again for the Anaheim Ducks on the other side of the Hudson River, as another slow start doomed the visitors on this ill-fated east coast road trip. Anaheim trailed 2-0 after a lackluster first period, and despite keeping New Jersey within arm’s reach and scoring midway through the third, the Devils held serve and held the game, 4-1, on Thursday at Prudential Center. The Ducks (4-6-0, eight points) have lost their fifth straight game and all three games to open this four-game road trip. Anaheim led after the first period in its first seven games of the season, but the Ducks have not led once in these three road games.“Obviously, losing isn't fun,” Jackson LaCombe said to local media, “but I think our compete got better throughout the game. We got to start the game moving our feet like that. As a group, we have to make that decision. It's frustrating." Tim Washe scored on a deflection of LaCombe’s third-period point shot with just under 12 minutes remaining to cut the lead to 2-1, but Anaheim generated just three shots on goal down the stretch. Arseny Gritsyuk scored in his fourth straight game, and Nico Hischier scored on a power play in the final minute of the first period for that 2-0 New Jersey lead. Anthony Mantha scored the Devils’ third goal–all from right on top of the crease–to answer Washe’s tip in, and Jack Hughes iced the game with an empty netter. “We competed a lot better for sure, but it can't be a 20 minute thing,” LaCombe said. “It's got to be the whole game. We keep leaving our goalies out to dry, too. We've got to help them out a lot more." Ville Husso stopped 25 of 28 shots in his third start for Anaheim. Nico Daws made 16 saves for the Devils. Anaheim concludes its four-game East Coast road trip with an emotional spark plug in Philadelphia on Saturday afternoon. The Ducks return home to host the Vancouver Canucks on Tuesday. "We're a little bit out of sorts,” Joel Quenneville said, “but it still felt like we had way more battle than we had the last couple of games tonight."Anaheim was forced to make another set of line-up changes entering Thursday, as defenseman Pavel Mintyukov returned to Orange County with a lower-body injury (day-to-day) and forward Jeff Malott was out due to illness. The Ducks were already without forward Judd Caulfield (returned to SoCal for birth of his child), center Ryan Poehling (6-8 weeks, MCL strain), defenseman Ian Moore (injured reserve, lower-body injury) and forward Troy Terry still out at least a month recovering from offseason hip surgery.“We got to be better than we are,” Quenneville said. “We're missing some guys. Some important guys that are not in our line up. We're missing a little bit of that, whether it's bite, whether it's experience..."

item.title: Bears 30, Patriots 24: Caleb Williams, Luther Burden III shine in prime time
item.description: (Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images) CHICAGO — Luther Burden III picked a prime time to come alive for the Bears . Burden finished with a season-high 130 receiving yards on four catches, all in the first half. On three-and-17 from the Patriots’ 24 with 21 seconds until halftime, he housed a tunnel screen from quarterback Caleb Williams . Williams followed up his Week 6 NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors with another exceptional performance, finishing 22-for-33 passing for 308 yards, two touchdowns and a 116.7 passer rating. Kicker Cairo Santos sealed the Bears’ 30-24 win with a career-long 58-yard field goal with less than two minutes remaining. Tight end Cole Kmet suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter and was carted to the locker room. Cornerback Malik Muhammad II exited the game in the third quarter with a toe injury. Neither returned. Tune in to the CHGO Bears Postgame show . The CHGO staff reacts to the win … Adam Hoge : The Bears made that win a lot harder than it needed to be, but the Patriots are a good team and never quit. Caleb Williams was excellent again and should still be in the MVP conversation. Cairo Santos’ 58-yard field goal was as clutch as it gets, especially after the miss. Adam Jahns : It might have been too crazy to be called a signature win. But it was still a darn good one for the Bears. They beat the defending AFC Champions and quarterback Drake Maye. Ben Johnson and Dennis Allen matched wits with Mike Vrabel and Josh McDaniels. And Caleb Williams played well again after coming back from his hamstring injury. Patrick Norton : That almost feels like the most satisfying win of the Bears’ young season. The moment wasn’t too big for anybody on the Bears’ sideline, and Caleb Williams is absolutely playing at an MVP level. And kudos to Cairo Santos. That had to feel good to drill it from 58 after a doink from 53. Mark Carman : Grind-it-out win on a short week by the resilient Bears. Caleb Williams was impressive with his arm and his legs on a short week. Rome Odunze struggled early, then came up with two huge catches late that helped put the Bears in position to win. Cairo Santos bounced back after a doink to nail his career-long 58-yard field goal. Daniel Hardy and ‘Marco Jackson were very solid in place of TJ Edwards. The 5-2 Bears now get a long weekend before they play again in 11 days at Seattle. Greg Braggs Jr : Five days, two wins. And the Chicago Bears are right on track. You could not have asked for a better start to the season considering everything they have overcome. Caleb Williams is back and quite literally better than ever. And now Ben Johnson gets a mini bye to get his team healthy for a very tough stretch in their schedule. One thing can be certain: throw out the Xs and Os, the way this team plays for each other shows they are one of the most dangerous teams in football. What a time to be alive.

item.title: Even the halftime performer was not safe from frustrated 76ers fans
item.description: John Jones-Imagn Images Even the halftime performer was not safe from frustrated 76ers fans appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Philadelphia 76ers successfully spoiled the New York Knicks on Right Night, but they were the ones who were on the verge of getting spoiled on their home opener against the Cleveland Cavaliers. The Cavs raced out to a massive lead over the Sixers in the first half and went into halftime leading by a whopping 24 points. Safe to say, Philly fans went into the break in a bad mood, and that wasn’t good news for the game’s halftime performance. The performer, whose act included twirling around an illuminated cube in the dark, got roundly booed by the Philly crowd . Philly fans have already booed the Sixers and the halftime performer at their home opener tonight. pic.twitter.com/HrkgVgrEgV Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Underdog NBA (@UnderdogNBA) October 23, 2026 Did they boo because they were frustrated by Philly’s poor play in the first half or because they really weren’t into his act, which didn’t look all that entertaining based on the brief clip of it? Perhaps a little bit of both. After their disappointing first-half showing, though, the Sixers ended up regrouping during the halftime break and they went into the second half on a mission. They outscored the Cavs 69-37 over the last two periods as they stormed to an incredible 114-106 comeback win. Tyrese Maxey once again starred for the Sixers as he finished with a team-high 32 points with six assists. Meanwhile, Joel Embiid got the better of his matchup against Jarrett Allen by dropping 24 points on 8-of-16 shooting. With the win, the Sixers improved to 2-0 on the season. They will look to make it three straight wins to start the season when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday. Hopefully, no halftime performer’s feelings will get hurt by booing fans again. item.description: What to Know WBA/WBO unified cruiserweight champion David Benavidez will take on WBC World Cruiserweight champion Michael Cieslak of Poland on Saturday, December 5, at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona. The card also features the long-awaited return of Vergil Ortiz Jr. , who moves up to the middleweight division to face former world champion Keith Thurman Jr . Undefeated star Vergil Ortiz Jr. returns after a lengthy absence and will make his middleweight division debut against former unified world champion Keith “One Time” Thurman. This followed his unification at light heavyweight in 2025. item.content:encoded: What to Know WBA/WBO unified cruiserweight champion David Benavidez will take on WBC World Cruiserweight champion Michael Cieslak of Poland on Saturday, December 5, at the Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona. The card also features the long-awaited return of Vergil Ortiz Jr. , who moves up to the middleweight division to face former world champion Keith Thurman Jr . Rising stars Emiliano Vargas and Marco Romero plus Australia’s Nikita Tszyu all join the fan-friendly card lineup. Undefeated WBA and WBO World Cruiserweight champion David “El Monstro” Benavidez will fight again in 2026. Benavidez (32-0, 26 KOs) will take on a high-stakes unification clash against WBC World Cruiserweight champion Michal Cieslak of Poland (28-2, 22 KOs) on Saturday, December 5. The event leads a PBC Pay-Per-View event available on DAZN through Prime Video from Desert Diamond Arena in Glendale, Arizona, starting at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT. Undefeated star Vergil Ortiz Jr. returns after a lengthy absence and will make his middleweight division debut against former unified world champion Keith “One Time” Thurman. Three exciting next-generation boxing stars who are quickly building fan followings also appear on the card: super lightweight Emiliano “El General” Vargas; rising middleweight star Marco “El Tiburon” Romero; and making his U.S. debut, unbeaten Australian star Nikita Tszyu opens the card in a super welterweight bout. Tickets for the live event go on sale Friday, October 23 at 12 noon PT through Ticketmaster.com . Benavidez Return – A Bid for Fighter of the Year? David Benavidez Jr. became the unified cruiserweight champion with his knockout win over Gilberto “Zurdo” Ramirez. Photo: Premier Boxing Champions A three-division world champion, David “El Monstro” Benavidez returns for his first fight back in Arizona since his 2022 destruction of David Lemieux. The 29-year-old Benavidez made his cruiserweight debut in style on Cinco de Mayo weekend in Las Vegas, dominating Gilberto Ramirez and stopping him in the sixth round to become the unified cruiserweight champion. This followed his unification at light heavyweight in 2025. A Phoenix native, Benavidez became the youngest-ever super middleweight world champion at 20, defeating Ronald Gavril by split decision for the vacant WBC title in 2017. “I’m excited to be fighting in Arizona once again,” said Benavidez. “It’s been a long time coming, but it’s finally here. I’m gonna give the fans in my home state of Arizona a great performance on December 5.” “‘The Mexican Monster’ David Benavidez hides from no one, and no one can stop him,” said Sampson Lewkowicz of Sampson Boxing. David has always had my full support for his history-making career. This is his time.” Michael Cieslak joins a long line of Polish cruiserweight world champions, including Tomasz Adamek, Krzysztof Wlodarczyk and Krzysztof Glowacki. Cieslak earned his belt with a fourth-round stoppage of former champion Jean Pascal in June 2025 in Pascal’s hometown. He won the interim title and was recently elevated. Cieslak is riding an impressive seven-fight winning streak, all wins by knockout. His only losses are by a close decision to Ilunga Makabu in 2020 and to Lawrence Okolie in 2022, “I’ve been waiting for this opportunity my whole life,” said Cieslak. “This is exactly why I’ve been training, to test myself and compete on the biggest stage against fighters like Benavidez. “I’m confident, but there’s no point in talking nonsense. The focus has to be on hard work. Those who know me understand that I’m not going there just to show up,” insists Cieslak. Long-Awaited Return of Vergil Ortiz Jr. Against a Familiar Face in Keith Thurman It will be 13 months since Vergil Ortiz Jr. stopped Erickson Lubin when he makes his ringwalk in Glendale on December 5. The undefeated Ortiz Jr. of Grand Prairie, Texas (24-0, 22 KOs) will shake off his ring rust against the former unified world champion Keith “One Time” Thurman of Clearwater, Florida (31-2, 23 KOs ) i n a 12-round middleweight. Trained by Robert Garcia, Ortiz Jr.has dominated his competition with his aggressive style, with notable victories over Maurice Hooker, Egidijus Kavaliauskas and top contender Serhii Bohachuk. In his last two bouts, he defeated Israil Madrimov in a wide decision before taking out former title contender Erickson Lubin in two rounds last November. “Being the co-main for Benavidez is an honor as I respect him equally as a fighter and a person,” said Ortiz Jr. “It’s gonna be a great night of boxing, and overall I’m just happy to be active again.” Thurman brings a resume with wins over former champions Shawn Porter, Danny Garcia and Robert Guerrero in high-profile fights. Thurman had a rough go against Sebastian Fundora last March, just his second loss as a professional. Now he will move up to middleweight to take on Ortiz Jr. “I’m back with a vengeance!” said Thurman. “I’m bringing the heat in December with an action fight against Vergil Ortiz, another young lion. Fans should really enjoy this one – you know the resume. I fight the best and the gladiator in me is not done yet. Get ready, Christmas is coming early.” “There’s a reason why Vergil Ortiz Jr. is the most avoided fighter without a belt,” said Golden Boy Chairman and CEO Oscar De La Hoya. “As a former world champion, Keith Thurman is a crafty, experienced fighter who has been in there with the very best and will give Vergil some good rounds.” Emiliano Vargas: Second Generation Talent Emiliano Vargas of Las Vegas (18-0, 15 KOs) is still early in his career, but he has the skills and the charisma to make it easy to picture him as a future world champion like his father Fernando Vargas. Vargas hopes to notch his third knockout win of 2025 in December. “This year has been a true blessing for me,” said Vargas. “I want to end this year on a high note by delivering a spectacular performance for my people and showing why I am ready to take on the biggest challenges of my career. Everything I’ve experienced this year motivates me to keep working even harder. ‘El General’ is coming with everything he’s got—and the best is yet to come!” Marco Romero Keeps Busy and Keeps Impressing Marco Romero gained invaluable experience while sparring with WBC Super Middleweight Champion Christian Mbilli in Montreal. Photo: Kansas Boxing Academy Just one week ago, Marco Romero of Overland Park, Kanas (16-0, 14 KOs) scored an impressive one punch knockout of Matias Ferreira on October 17. He plans to build on his momentum on the December 5 card. Romero has gained top-level experience after recently making his second training visit to Montreal to spar with super middleweight champions Christian Mbilli and Osleys Iglesias. “I’m excited to come right back, which shows me how much PBC believes in me, especially by putting me on another big card like this,” said Romero. “Being on his card because so many Latinos will be there or watching because of Benavidez can only help me. A platform like this is perfect for me.” Nikita Tszyu Eager to Introduce Himself to American Fans Nikita Tszyu will follow in father Kostya’s footsteps in Glendale, Arizona. Photo: No-Limit Boxing The son of former unified champion Kostya and younger brother of former champion Tim Tszyu, Nikita Tszyu (12-0-1, 10 KOs) looks to carry his family’s legacy. The 28-year-old Sydney native has beaten previously undefeated Lulzim Ismaili and Oscar Diaz, and owns a stoppage win over Koen Mazoudier. “To be on a massive David Benavidez card is truly an honor. He’s the most exciting fighter in the world. He comes forward, he hurts people, and he never gives anyone an easy night. That’s the kind of fighting I respect,” said Tszyu. “Arizona is also where my father had his last victory, so it holds an important place in my heart. It will be special to write the next chapter of our family’s story there.” Opponents for Vargas, Romero, and Tszyu will be named later.

item.title: Adam Schefter Reveals New Twist In Sam LaPorta’s Standoff With Lions
item.description: Sam LaPorta Getty Lions' head coach Dan Campbell revealed that Sam LaPorta is likely out for the season with a back injury Getty Detroit Lions tight end Sam LaPorta found himself in the headlines recently when he offered an unfiltered opinion on the lack of a new contract beyond this current season on the “Pardon My Take” podcast, implying that if the Lions won’t pay him, then he’ll go elsewhere to get what he feels is a fair contract. And now, according to a top NFL Insider, it appears as though LaPorta will eventually get his new contract, but it won’t be until after the current campaign. New Twist Emerges In Sam LaPorta Saga With Detroit Lions Getty Lions’ head coach Dan Campbell revealed that Sam LaPorta is likely out for the season with a back injury According to NFL Insider Adam Schefter, LaPorta will be paid, but it won’t be until after the 2026 season. “Eventually, Sam LaPorta is going to get paid. But it looks like now it will NOT be until after this season,” Schefter said on ESPN earlier on Thursday. So far, talks between the two sides have not produced the kind of deal that LaPorta thought that he’d be getting. While there’s still time to get a deal done, it now looks like such a deal won’t be coming until after the season based on what Schefter had to say on Thursday. Sam LaPorta Ripped The Lack Of An Extension During a recent appearance on the “Pardon My Take” podcast, LaPorta offered an unfiltered take, expressing his extreme frustration over what he felt was a lack of progress on a contract. “I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport that we play, it sucks,” LaPorta said . “And it’s disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt. Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f***ing back for the team. And then I’m going out there this year, and I’m balling, and maybe they’re just not showing the love. “So it sucks. I’m going to continue to be a pro, and I dish a lot of that to my agent, and he handles that great. … So I’m going to continue to go do my thing and ball out. And in three months, if I don’t get to wear the Honolulu Blue and play for the Lions anymore, it’s going to be all good. I’ll go get paid somewhere else.” This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Adam Schefter Reveals New Twist In Sam LaPorta’s Standoff With Lions appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: NBA legend Jason Kidd gets 100% real about whether he could dominate in today’s era
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images NBA legend Jason Kidd gets 100% real about whether he could dominate in today’s era appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jason Kidd has moved from the sideline to the studio , and he is not shy about how he thinks he would fare in today’s NBA. Appearing on ESPN’s “Tip-Off” show , the Hall of Fame point guard was asked by Kenny Smith how a 22-year-old version of himself would handle the modern league, given how differently the game is played now. Kidd did not hesitate. “Well, if you’re asking me, if I were coming in today, yes, just the speed of the game,” Kidd said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jason Kidd believes a 22-year-old version of himself would dominate today’s NBA: “The speed of the game… I would love to be playing this time of the year, in this generation… If I was playing now, I think I could dominate.” pic.twitter.com/7XY01otXB9 — NBABase (@TheNBABase) October 22, 2026 The 53-year-old explained that the style of play he grew up in looked very different. Back then, offenses often revolved around getting the ball to a dominant big man. “In the ’80s and ’90s, if I was playing with Shaq, you know, our job, you play with the incredible center on a team. We got to wait for him,” Kidd said. “We got to let him get the ball. We got to get him touches. And then we’ll play off of the big.” Now, the game is built around pace and spacing, with teams launching threes at a historic rate. Kidd believes that would have suited him perfectly. “The game has changed. A lot more threes,” Kidd said. “Everyone’s shooting the three. I would love to be playing this time of the year, in this generation.” He also pointed to the return of physical defense as something he would welcome. “Hopefully, as you can see, we’re starting to maybe get back to that without hurting someone. But it’s all right to be physical, to guard defensively,” Kidd said. “And so hopefully, if I was playing now, I think I could dominate.” Kidd certainly has the resume to back up the confidence. He was one of the best playmakers of his generation, earning 10 All-Star selections and winning a championship with the Dallas Mavericks in 2011 before being inducted into the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. His comments come as he settles into a new role. Kidd joined ESPN as a studio analyst for the 2026-27 season after parting ways with the Mavericks, whom he coached for five seasons and led to the 2024 NBA Finals. Now, instead of drawing up plays, Kidd will be breaking them down on television. item.title: 76ers make history with stunning comeback win vs. Cavs
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images 76ers make history with stunning comeback win vs. Cavs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers saw the energy drain inside Xfinity Mobile Arena by falling behind by 29 points. Tyrese Maxey even engaged in a shoving match with ex-Sixer James Harden . But Philly fought back and made NBA history on Thursday night against the Cleveland Cavaliers. The 76ers stormed back in epic fashion to win 114-106. And in the process have rewritten the history books in the NBA. “The Sixers are are the first team in NBA history to overcome a 20+ point halftime deficit to win their home opener,” the account OptaSTATS posted on the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Cleveland raced to a 69-45 lead at the half, drawing out the boo birds inside the arena. And the Cavs jumped out to that lead in the 76ers home debut of LeBron James . But Philly and coach Nick Nurse got the Sixers to clamp down on defense in impressive fashion. The Sixers bottled the Cavs to a combined 37 second half points, as Philly outscored them 74-37 the rest of the way. Furthermore, this now becomes the 76ers’ largest comeback victory since the 1997-98 season . That’s also the year Cleveland blew its biggest lead in a single game. But more astonishing for Philly? The 76ers rise as the first team in 66 tries to wipe away a 20+ point halftime deficit and win their home season opener. Tyrese Maxey dropped 32 points and dished out six assists to lead the way. Joel Embiid delivered 24 points including banking this late basket on one leg. Joel Embiid hits the one-legged fade over Jarrett Allen for 24 points 🔥 Sixers lead the Cavs by 6 with 2:11 left. pic.twitter.com/yy9CTjN03Z — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 23, 2026 Jaylen Brown also had his own home debut for Philly , scoring 21 points after coming over via the Boston Celtics by trade. James put together the double-double of 17 points with 10 rebounds. item.title: Former Luka Doncic Teammate Predicts 80 Point Game Vs Yaxel
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 21: Yaxel Lendeborg #1 of the Golden State Warriors defends against Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers during the first half of a game at Crypto.com Arena on October 21, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) Getty The bad blood between Luka Doncic and Yaxel Lendeborg remains one of the top stories of NBA opening week. Doncic’s Los Angeles Lakers destroyed the Golden State Warriors on Wednesday, but fans were more taken back by the epic trash talk. Luka claimed that Yaxel started, and he was inspired to get the better of the rookie. However, Lendeborg took it further by stating he has no respect for Doncic after seeing how he behaves in person. Former Luka teammate Naji Marshall commented on a social media post and made a bold prediction for the next time they play: “80 ball next time they play never speak on the DON ” Marshall is predicting that Doncic will have a historic 80-point performance to embarrass Lendeborg and the Warriors. History has shown Luka holding grudges with the Phoenix Suns and other teams when their players talk enough trash to upset him. The time together on the Dallas Mavericks saw Doncic and Marshall becoming good friends on and off the court. Marshall is one of many former Luka teammates to still have his back on different teams. Doncic’s track record does make it logical that he will have an epic performance next time he has a chance to publicly humble Yaxel again. item.title: Steve Young Reveals Why He’s ‘Worried’ About the San Francisco 49ers
item.description: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - JANUARY 03: Former quarterback Steve Young of the San Francisco 49ers looks on prior to a game against the Seattle Seahawks at Levi's Stadium on January 03, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Lachlan Cunningham/Getty Images) Getty The San Francisco 49ers are one of just three remaining undefeated teams in the NFL. They’re coming off a 23-17 victory over the Washington Commanders on Monday night that improved their record to 6-0. However, the 49ers have continued to deal with injuries across the roster. They’ve navigated those issues through training camp, the preseason and the first six weeks of the regular season. Steve Young ‘Worried’ About 49ers While many believe the 49ers are Super Bowl favorites, Hall of Fame quarterback and San Francisco legend Steve Young still has concerns about the team’s current state, particularly whether it can stay healthy. “I think we should stand on the shoes. Especially with the Rams 2-4, and the Seahawks… they’re both kind of reeling in a way right now. But that’s fine. Let’s stand on those shoes,” Young said about the 49ers being labeled Super Bowl favorites during an appearance on KNBR. “But let’s also recognize out of 12 halves that I’ve seen played. The last half is what puts me with a little shiver. We get people hurt, we’re not full speed, we don’t have everyone on the field… but I just worry… I still worry. So I want to stay a worried tone because I know that the games that are coming towards the end of the season are the ones that decide it and I just want us locked in. If we go 17-0 that’s great. I don’t want to look back, I don’t want to take the foot off the pedal, I want to sprint to as many wins as we can and then be as healthy as we can. “If everyone can just stay healthy, we’re gonna be in the mix.” Steve Young is still worried. The 49ers are 6-0, but last week’s second half gave him “shivers.” (via Dirty Work w/ @Adamcopes & @dpapapops) https://t.co/jvzG0JBQ6j — KNBR (@KNBR) October 22, 2026 Looking at the 49ers San Francisco has been led by quarterback Brock Purdy, who’s playing at an MVP level and producing across the offense. A key piece of his success has been veteran wide receiver Mike Evans, who’s had to battle through several injuries. His health has become a concern for some 49ers fans this early in the season. However, San Francisco has managed to go 6-0 without several key players. Star pass rusher Nick Bosa has missed several weeks, the team is down multiple wide receivers, and several other players are still working their way back. Despite all the injuries, the 49ers remain undefeated and still have plenty of room to improve once they get closer to full strength. item.title: LeBron James’ Philadelphia connection dates back 24 years with Kobe Bryant impression
item.description: Photo by Jeff Gross/Getty Images LeBron James’ connection to Philadelphia stretches back nearly 24 years before he made his home debut for the 76ers, with the NBA legend once starring in a high school game at the city’s famous Palestra arena. James was still an 18-year-old prospect when St. Vincent–St. Mary High School faced Strawberry Mansion in December 2002. The future NBA superstar scored 28 points as his team secured an emphatic 85-47 victory. Now beginning a new chapter with the Sixers, James has another opportunity to experience the passion of Philadelphia’s basketball fans from the home side. LeBron James once drew comparisons to Kobe Bryant in Philadelphia The high school game was organised by Jeremy Treatman, who had watched James play at a tournament in Delaware and wanted Philadelphia fans to see the young star for themselves. Treatman, who had been an assistant coach at Lower Merion during Kobe Bryant’s high school career, was already convinced James had something special. Recalling his first impression, Treatman said: “I think I just saw somebody as good as, if not better than Kobe.” The game at the Palestra sold out, with Treatman claiming that around 1,000 additional spectators managed to get inside. James delivered a performance to remember, finishing with eight rebounds, five assists and seven steals alongside his 28 points. Allen Iverson was also reportedly in attendance as the highly rated teenager showcased the talent that would eventually make him one of basketball’s biggest names. James reflected on that experience during his introductory press conference as a Philadelphia 76er, explaining that he was familiar with the intensity of the city’s supporters. He said: “It’s been like, OK, we respect the way you play the game because we know the game and we know the history of the game and we’ve seen so many players play. But we hate you, you know like, you’re not with us and we hate you. But I love that, I actually really thrive under that circumstance.” James also recalled his previous appearance at the Palestra, adding: “I actually came here in high school as well and played at the Palestra my senior year. And it was that same type of atmosphere, you know. Happy to be on this side, though.” His first home appearance for Philadelphia saw the 76ers beat Cleveland 114-106. James finished with 17 points, 10 rebounds and five assists as he began settling into life with his new team. item.title: Bears Jersey Patch: Why Is No. 89 on Chicago’s Uniforms?
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - OCTOBER 18: D'Andre Swift #4 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after defeating the Atlanta Falcons in the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on October 18, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty The Chicago Bears are wearing distinct jersey patches with the No. 89 as a new addition to the team’s uniforms. Why are the Bears wearing the No. 89 jersey patches and what is the meaning? Chicago is no stranger to having different jersey patches, but the newest addition is to honor the team’s former head coach Mike Ditka. The former Bears player and coach wore the No. 89 during his time with Chicago. Ditka died on October 9, 2026, at the age of 86. Ditka passed away less than two weeks before his 87th birthday. Following Ditka’s death, the Bears announced plans to wear the No. 89 jersey patches for the remainder of the 2026 season. Here’s what you need to know about the Bears’ new jersey patches with the No. 89. Bears Legend Mike Ditka Died on October 9, at the Age of 86 Additionally, the Bears have the letters “GSH” on the team’s shoulder pads in honor of the team’s founder George Stanley Halas Sr. The franchise released a statement reflecting on Ditka’s impact following his death. “We are deeply saddened by the passing of legendary and treasured Chicago Bear and Pro Football Hall of Famer Mike Ditka,” the Bears said in an October 12, statement. “Mike’s impact on the Chicago Bears organization, over decades as a player, coach, and proud icon and ambassador for our organization, is immeasurable. His integral role in bringing world championships to our city and our franchise, both as a player and as our coach, established prominence and excellence at a world-class level, but also created a lifetime of cherished memories in the hearts and minds of Bears fans that will last for generations,” the statement continued. “”We extend our love, prayers, and heartfelt condolences to the Ditka family, and join all Bears fans in deep sadness and reverence as we remember and honor Mike Ditka.” Bears Jersey Patches: A History of Chicago’s Uniforms, Including No. 89 At different points in the franchise history, the Bears have worn various patches. During the 2025 season, the Bears wore a “VHM” patch in honor of the late principal owner Virginia Halas McCaskey. item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Bournemouth enjoy night to remember as 10-man Milan fail to weather storm
item.description: This was a momentous night in Bournemouth’s history, although the truth is they would have been given a far sterner examination by Coventry or Hull. Whatever this rotten impersonation of a Milan side was, it bore no relation to those that forged such a celebrated history. The visitors resembled holograms even before their goalkeeper Mike Maignan, with an extraordinary rush of blood resulting in a penalty and red card, rendered their task impossible. They never showed the slightest hint of putting up a fight. Bournemouth simply swamped the seven-time European champions and, amid a swirling south coast storm that rarely let up, could depart singing in the rain. Amine Adli’s sumptuous late free-kick, curled left-footed from 22 yards, meant they could finish the evening with the flourish they deserved. Their joy was clear at full time and met disapproval from some of Milan’s staff, who appeared to take umbrage in a short-lived fracas near the tunnel afterwards. Continue reading...

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022 ? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn.
